_comment: GENERATED by scripts/compute-period-keyness.mjs. Dunning G2 keyness per root per revelation period, tested against random assignment of whole surahs to periods. Conditional on the Noldeke-Bell four-period chronology in data/chronology.json, one scheme among several.
source: Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus v0.4 (GPL); data/chronology.json

method.statistic: Dunning G2 over the token-level 2x2 (root in period / root elsewhere), all Leeds tokens as the universe
method.null: assign the 114 surahs to the four periods at random keeping each period's number of surahs; 100,000 draws, mulberry32 seed 20261018
method.p: (1 + draws with G2 >= observed) / (100000 + 1); smallest possible 1e-5
method.q: Benjamini-Hochberg over all 6568 root-period tests; passing = q <= 0.05
method.direction: enriched when the root's rate in the period exceeds its rate elsewhere, else depleted

calibration.method: 40 random relabelings of the surahs stand in for the observed chronology; each is tested against 5,000 fresh draws with the same BH step (seed 20261019)
calibration.note: Because each pseudo-chronology is itself a draw from the null, tests passing BH here are false positives. Roots share surahs, so the tests are strongly dependent: false positives arrive in bursts (several roots at once when one large surah lands in a period) rather than one at a time. The share of runs with any passing test estimates how often a whole-chronology analysis would report something in noise; Benjamini-Hochberg is designed to keep that near the 0.05 level. The p-value floor is 1/(draws + 1), so the calibration runs with fewer draws are the harder case.
